author: Josephine Ma
description:
Trita Parsi is co-founder and executive vice-president of the Quincy Institute, a Washington-based think tank. He is an expert on US-Iranian relations, Iranian foreign policy and the geopolitics of the Middle East. He has written four books on US foreign policy in the Middle East, with a particular focus on Iran and Israel. Born in Iran, Parsi moved to Sweden with his family as a child and then to the United States as an adult.
This interview first appeared in SCMP Plus. For other interviews in...
title: Trita Parsi on why US air strikes strengthened Iran’s hand and failed to trigger a revolt

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
The People’s Liberation Army is increasingly embracing broader “systems-oriented warfare” rather than relying on individual weapons platforms – a shift Taiwanese analysts say could pose new challenges to the island’s defences.
Instead of focusing on individual weapons, the PLA has progressively emphasised integrating intelligence, AI, communications, weapons, logistics and infrastructure into an overall combat system, they warn.
“The PLA is no longer concerned only with whose weapons are...
title: PLA shift to systems warfare means Taiwan’s defences need to change: experts

author: Zhou Xiaoming
description:
Earlier this month, when US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened sanctions against any nation continuing to purchase Iranian crude oil, he did not name China. He did not need to. China, the Islamic Republic’s largest oil customer, is squarely in Washington’s crosshairs.
The US has already unveiled new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels linked to Iranian trade, including some in mainland China and Hong Kong. Just three months after the May summit between President Xi...
title: Will US threats over Iran be the last straw for Beijing?

author: Shi Huang
description:
For many, losing hair isn’t just a cosmetic worry – it is a deeply personal struggle that can chip away at confidence, social life and mental health. Now, a surprising candidate is offering new hope: a pill originally designed to treat arthritis.
The condition is called alopecia areata. It is an autoimmune disease where the body’s own immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, causing unpredictable hair loss. Sometimes it is just a few patches but in severe cases, the entire scalp,...
title: Arthritis drug restores 100% of hair on some patients with severe alopecia in global trial

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Shanghai has named career finance official Zhu Zhongming as the municipal government’s new party chief, an appointment that puts him in line to become the city’s next mayor.
The appointment was announced on Saturday in a social media post that said he had chaired a meeting of the city government’s party leadership group.
Zhu replaces the current mayor, Gong Zheng, in the post. However, the city’s most senior position is that of the secretary of the Shanghai Communist Party committee, which is...
title: Career finance official moves into pole position to become Shanghai’s next mayor

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Uzbekistan confirmed that it has become the second foreign country to acquire the J-10CE fighter, as Beijing makes inroads into a Central Asian market previously dominated by Russian warplanes.
Reports had previously suggested Uzbekistan had ordered 24 J-10CEs, although neither country has confirmed the deal.
However, at least six of the jets were shown in footage released by the Uzbek president’s office on Friday as part of the country’s independence day celebrations.
The footage showed the...
title: Uzbekistan confirmed as second country to buy China’s J-10CE fighter

author: Jane Cai,Caroline Lin
description:
In the quiet of a Peking University research room, shelves groan under the weight of 60 thick volumes. Stacked, they stand taller than an average human.
Inside their pages lie the details of more than 23,000 ancient Chinese bronze vessels, weapons, chariot fittings and ritual objects that left China’s shores long ago and now sit in museums, private collections and auction houses across nearly 30 countries.
Published in April by Shanghai Classics Publishing House, the Collection of Chinese...
title: 23,000 bronzes, 14 years, 60 volumes: how China is mapping lost heritage held abroad

author: Orange Wang
description:
China and the Philippines have been urged to resume joint South China Sea energy exploration as a way of easing tensions in the disputed waters.
A joint report by Chinese and Philippine analysts also said the two countries should work together in other “low-sensitivity” areas such as marine environmental protection and combating crime at sea.
The report, published on Monday by the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies think tank, said the relationship between the two countries was at a...
title: Could joint oil and gas projects help ease Beijing and Manila’s South China Sea tensions?

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
The Chinese authorities said on Sunday that 261 foreign citizens were missing after last week’s deadly floods along the border between Tibet and Nepal.
The Tibetan authorities said that the missing foreigners were from 23 different countries and included 104 Nepalese citizens.
They also included 49 from India; 33 Latvians; 18 from the United States; 15 from Britain; six each from Canada and Australia; four from South Africa; three each from Malaysia, Germany and Russia; two from Ireland,...
title: China-Nepal floods: hundreds of foreigners missing in Tibet after disaster

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Friction between humans and wild animals at China’s Giant Panda National Park intensified significantly over the past decade as conservation efforts expanded, a new study has found.
Farmers reported increasing losses between 2015 and 2024 stemming from damage to property and crops as well as attacks on humans and livestock.
The team behind the study said the issue had become the most prominent challenge facing the park’s administrators.
The Giant Panda National Park covers 22,000 sq km (8,500 sq...
title: Human-wild animal clashes on the rise in China’s Giant Panda National Park
